domain: multi-layer workflow-orchestration topology and subsumption analysis
axioms: A new orchestration component is guilty of redundancy until proven innocent — the default posture toward a proposed new layer is suspicion, not acceptance
A layer boundary is only real if drawn on a stable axis (lifecycle stage, fan-out granularity, session vs sub-task scope) — naming two systems differently does not make them different layers

Exactly one system must own in-flight state for any given concern (dispatch concurrency, artifact location, completion status); two systems independently tracking the same state is a drift hazard even if their APIs never directly conflict

Refusing to build a needed thin layer because an adjacent system 'could' technically do it produces a worse outcome (Frankenstein integration) than building the layer — subsumption avoidance is not costless

An unstarted/OPEN dependency (lbkd) forces its own subsumption answer the moment a consuming system's v1 needs the capability it would provide — deferring the question does not defer the sequencing hazard

Consumption model (event-driven vs poll, staged/escrowed vs immediate spawn, library vs command) is itself a variable that can change which subsumption answer is correct, not a downstream implementation detail
primitives: channel ownership (which system is source of truth for a given piece of in-flight state)
consumption model (event-driven, poll, escrowed/staged fan-out, immediate spawn)
subsumption relation (dependency / subsumed / orthogonal / consumer / different-layer / same-thing-rediscovered)
session vs sub-task vs goal scope boundary
failure_mode: Accepts a naming distinction (Rimsky vs Mycroft, Rimsky vs the artifact bus) as evidence of a real layer boundary without checking whether the underlying state/channel is actually singly-owned

Under-weights cost-economics and control-theory detail (exact crossover thresholds, gate falsifiability) that belongs to a different lens — can misjudge the SEVERITY of a subsumption ambiguity if the resolution depends on a measurement plan rather than a structural argument

May over-index on prior-art shape (Mycroft's existing suggest/approve loop) as the template for what Rimsky 'must' avoid duplicating, missing genuinely novel orchestrator shapes that don't map cleanly onto either existing system's topology
